Interface ParameterizedSql

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
All Known Subinterfaces:
SqlQuery<B>, SqlStatement
public interface ParameterizedSql extends AutoCloseable
A single SQL operation bound to its arguments, which prepares JDBC resources lazily and owns every resource it opens.

Constructing an operation performs no database work: the connection and PreparedStatement are acquired on first use and released by close(). The terminal methods on the subinterfaces — SqlStatement.execute(), SqlQuery.getSingleResult(), SqlQuery.getFirstRecord(), and SqlQuery.getResults() — close their own resources, so those calls need no surrounding try-with-resources. Every other entry point leaves resources open for continued reading and therefore requires the caller to close the operation: 

try (var query = dao.getQuery(MyBean.class, sql, args)) {
        final var page = query.getResults(100);
        // ...
}

Instances are stateful and are not safe for concurrent use by multiple threads.

    • getQuery

      String getQuery()
      Gets the SQL text this operation was created with, verbatim.

      SQL text; never null

    • getArguments

      Iterable<?> getArguments()
      Gets the bind arguments in placeholder order.
      Returns:
      unmodifiable argument values; empty when the SQL has no placeholders

    • getPreparedStatement

      PreparedStatement getPreparedStatement()
      Opens a connection if one is not already held, prepares the SQL, and binds getArguments().

      Each call discards and closes any statement and connection from a previous call, so the returned reference must not be retained across invocations. The returned statement remains owned by this operation and is closed by close(); callers must not close it directly.

      Returns:
      prepared JDBC statement, positioned before execution
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the connection cannot be obtained or the SQL cannot be prepared

    • close

      void close()
      Releases the JDBC resources held by this operation.

      Closing is idempotent and never throws: failures encountered while releasing resources are discarded so that they cannot mask an application failure already in flight. After closing, the operation may be used again, which re-prepares the SQL against a new connection.

      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
